Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers

OpenRouter 11/22/2026

Provider security announcements Provider security announcements

Earlier this week, security researchers reported that certain inference providers had data compromised or otherwise shown evidence that their data policies were not being upheld. We have been collaborating closely with the researchers and with providers to understand the findings and encourage the providers to address them.

These findings did not show any breach or unauthorized access of OpenRouter. The results of this testing revealed new findings about specific inference providers. A live list of the security announcements we have received from providers is below .

As the operating layer between customers and a fast-moving ecosystem of models and providers, we take data policy enforcement very seriously. We have taken the following actions:

Off-boarded three providers from OpenRouter, based on the results of our investigations.

Removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility. The removals included providers flagged by researchers, plus additional endpoints that we removed as a precautionary measure.

Notified all potentially affected customers.

The following work is underway:

We are adapting the researchers’ testing approach so we can run these checks on an ongoing basis.

We are conducting technical verification of network paths to identify instances where requests and responses may be being forwarded to third parties.

We are requiring appropriate assurances and validation before restoring ZDR eligibility to any endpoint removed in this review.

We are grateful for the Dragos report. As we integrate similar testing techniques into OpenRouter, we will keep raising the bar, and providers that want to be on OpenRouter will need to meet it.

Provider security announcements

Novita: Privacy notice regarding MiniMax requests on Novita

Phala: November preliminary incident report

Together: Security event: prompt leakage for requests in June and July of 2026

Not all affected providers have posted publicly. We have notified affected users regardless of whether there is a public post. We are encouraging all providers to create incident write-ups and will keep this list updated.

Subscribe

By subscribing you agree to receive the OpenRouter newsletter: model usage data, product updates, and research reports, about one email a week. Unsubscribe anytime via the link in every email. See our Privacy Policy .

Skip to content

Research / 2026 CVE-2026-125396

Upload 2Shell

A use-after-free in Ghostscript’s Type 1 font loader lets a crafted document cross Ghostscript’s -dSAFER sandbox, alter native path controls, and execute attacker-chosen commands as the rendering process.

Ghostscript sits beneath print, email, upload, and preview workflows. Our ImageMagick research showed how files named .png or .jpg can still reach Ghostscript through image conversion. The index below records confirmed affected paths alongside additional applications whose renderer routes we traced.

Explore application paths ↘
Read the technical writeup ↗

Upload2Shell / public record

Disclosure sequence

From the first escape to the downstream reports, fixes, and publication.

27 JUL 2026 DISCOVERY

Upload2Shell

We found a Type 1 font-loader path out of Ghostscript's -dSAFER boundary. A crafted document gained native access inside the rendering process.

BY 30 JUL GOOGLE PROOF

Google's image and document pipeline

A signed-out request for an attacker-hosted file reached Ghostscript in Google's document renderer. We sent the production proof to Google.

12 AUG 2026 WORDPRESS FIX

WordPress Core

Core's upload path exposed the renderer to Author+ users and any Contributor granted upload_files . Public upload fields in multiple plugins required no WordPress login. WordPress shipped its separate CVE-2026-65640 fix.

BY 02 SEP UPSTREAM REPORT

Artifex received the Ghostscript root

We filed the Type 1 loader flaw upstream as Artifex Bug 709684. Our broader audit also produced other independent Ghostscript findings.

08 SEP 2026 UPSTREAM RELEASE

Ghostscript 10.08.0

Artifex released the fix for the Type 1 loader flaw.

BY 09 SEP OTHER GHOSTSCRIPT ROOT

Dropbox

We confirmed a production document-processing finding in our broader Ghostscript research. Its individual root and proof belong to a separate case study.

12 SEP 2026 DISTRIBUTION UPDATE

Debian packaged the upstream release

Ghostscript 10.08.0 entered Debian unstable. The Debian 13 security update followed later.

17 SEP · 23:53 ET DEBIAN REPORT

Debian 13 CUPS

Confirmed unauthenticated remote command execution: an IPP job to a shared queue ran on the host as lp . We sent the network reproduction to Debian Security.

18 SEP · 00:25 ET ROUNDCUBE REPORT

Roundcube

Confirmed remote execution after an external sender's attachment was thumbnailed when its email was viewed. The tested ImageMagick delegate ran the proof as www-data .

18 SEP · 00:26 ET PLESK REPORT

Plesk Obsidian

Confirmed command execution in the Roundcube thumbnail path shipped with Plesk Obsidian. We reported the result to WebPros.

18 SEP · 00:26 ET ELEMENTOR REPORT

Essential Addons for Elementor

Confirmed unauthenticated remote command execution through a public registration widget with an upload field enabled. We reported the route to the plugin team.

18 SEP · 00:28 ET FORMINATOR REPORT

Forminator

Confirmed unauthenticated remote command execution

title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
desc: Signal 限制了用户在 Android 和 iOS 应用程序中截取屏幕截图的能力。
content:
In Brief

Posted:

1:37 PM PST · November 21, 2026

Image Credits: Matthias Balk/picture alliance / Getty Images

Anthony Ha

Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance

Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”

Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would break our privacy guarantees. She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”

NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia, whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week.

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia, a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing.

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

(Reporting by Chris Prentice in New York and Alexandra Alper in Washington; Additional reporting by Karen Freif

Introducing Inkling 2 Mini

Nov 20, 2026

Try on Tinker Hugging Face Model card

Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

title: Restricting AI agents in mobile operating systems platforms from capturing data
desc:
Article URL: https://signal.org/blog/protecting-your-privacy/
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50572348
Points: 525
# Comments: 310
content:
Signal is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy

Meredith Whittaker

on 20 Nov 2026

Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it.

This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially capturing and storing your Signal data.

We’ve already had to do this once with Windows. Last year, we used screenshot blocking to prevent Microsoft’s Recall AI from taking and storing screenshots of your Signal messages on Windows 11 operating systems by default. 1 We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen. 2

The problem is similar to Microsoft Recall on Windows: Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems. This is a significant move. Google (Android), Apple (iOS/macOS), and Microsoft (Windows) produce the three major consumer operating systems (OS), which comprise the environment that third-party developers – like Signal – build their apps to function and operate within. To put it differently, these three operating systems are the oceans in which Signal, and other applications, must swim; they dictate the conditions of life for the application ecosystem. Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.

In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents “scan” the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding.

The net result is that these AI capabilities in the operating system are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy. For over a decade, this guarantee has been backed by our tried and trusted open source code base and our formally verified encryption protocol. These have been scrutinized by some of the best security experts and hackers across the world, and shown to be robust. Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment. All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.

So, we are blocking such capture by preventing screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android. 2

People who want the ability to take screenshots can disable this protection within the Signal app’s settings. However, doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content

title: Daniel Ek backs AI researchers fusion power startup. Heres what theyre building.
desc: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.
content:
Image Credits: David M. Benett/Dave Benett / Getty Images

Climate

Daniel Ek backs AI researcher s fusion power startup. Here s what they re building.

Tim De Chant

11:53 AM PST · November 20, 2026

Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a stealthy fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher who is taking a different approach to developing a fusion power plant.

The U.K.-based startup was founded in February, though sources told TechCrunch that the founder, Nantas Nardelli, has been working on the idea for longer. The people asked not to be identified because the information isn’t public. Bloomberg first reported Ek’s backing of Europa Fusion.

Nardelli has extensive experience in the AI world, having previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Recently, he was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion , the fusion power startup based in Fremont, California.

Pacific Fusion recently broke ground on a demonstration facility in New Mexico. Like most fusion startups of its size , Pacific Fusion leans heavily on physical devices to test its theories and improve its simulations.

Nardelli apparently didn’t agree with the focus on hardware, instead thinking that fusion startups should invest in a more simulation- and data-heavy approach, a source familiar with his thinking told TechCrunch.

Like Pacific Fusion, Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed-power approach to fusion. Pulsed-power reactors use massive, perfectly timed surges of electrical current to compress fuel targets until the atoms inside fuse and release energy.

Fusion power has the potential to be a significant energy source in the coming decades, but to date, no one has built a power plant capable of supplying electricity to the grid. If fusion power becomes commercially viable, though, it could possibly be a significant source of carbon-free power that draws on nearly limitless fuel supplies. The technology also has the potential to alleviate concerns about AI’s energy consumption.

Fusion’s ability to generate electricity without exacerbating climate change apparently drove Nardelli’s pivot from AI.

“My original background is in electronics and control engineering,” he wrote on his website . “I used to build robots for a living. One day I’ll be back to that, but it s time to fix climate change for good.”

title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too
desc: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.
content:
Image Credits: andresr (opens in a new window) / Getty Images

AI

AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too

Tim Fernholz

11:32 AM PST · November 20, 2026

It s a big week for Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics.

The precise timing is horrible, he wrote in an essay announcing his findings and describing how he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last Sunday night to ask how to announce that he had found a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis, which dates back to 1859 and is among the Millennium Prize math problems.

The hypothesis conjectures that there is a hidden structure underlying the appearance of prime numbers. If the claimed result holds true, we re entering sublime-mysteries-of-the-universe territory.

Maybe the best way to understand how exciting this is to the mathematics community is to watch the experts puzzling through the result in a chat on Zulip . Mathematicians like Chris Birkbeck, a number theorist at the University of East Anglia, are posting thoughts like this

The cohomology bound is proved by what looks like an automorphy-lifting argument. It genuinely uses the existence of Galois representations attached to regular algebraic, polarized cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over CM fields, along with base change, Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel s purity, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, the main theorem of CM, Deligne–Ribet and more.

For my part, I tapped out of mathematics at college calculus, so I can t help decode exactly what that means.

But that comment was followed by 20 readers reacting 🤯.

It will be a while before the mathematics community feels like it has a handle on the proof, but most appear confident that the formalized Lean result will hold. Lean is an an open-source coding language used to express mathematical ideas as code, allowing proofs to be formally verified. Several participants in the Zulip chat, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, say they have successfully confirmed that Alpöge s solution can be compiled successfully.

Alpöge appeared in his essay to feel a bit guilty about releasing the proof without a truly human-intelligible explanation, but his obsession with the problem since childhood made him feel he could not live if he waited to release the finding.

Alpöge described a stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument through incredible confusion with Claude with more than a hint of AI euphoria, describing how the model flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.

However, for all that action to mean anything, we ll have to wait for humans to be able to understand the result and explain it to each other, something Alpöge has committed to pursue.

Image Credits: STR/NurPhoto / Getty Images

AI

Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac

Lucas Ropek

4:56 PM PST · November 19, 2026

Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.

The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an AI agent that can use a computer.

Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does, the posting says. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.

The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move fluidly between tools and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.

TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the company is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.

The outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.

Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year, progress on its in-house agent remains in the early stages.

title: Anthropics 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
desc: At the upgraded $83/share IPO price, Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million, while the company nabbed nearly $105 billion.
content:
Image Credits: CHARLY TRIBALLEAU/AFP / Getty Images

AI

Anthropic s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO

Julie Bort

4:43 PM PST · November 19, 2026

Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic s original price range. So that s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.

With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.

$104.8 billion. That s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.

28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

More than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company s need for future capital is still far greater.

Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ende

Related articles

Investigating vault particles with Claude

View more

Claude has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity. In the first, it completed a calculation that physicists set up more than 20 years ago, but which had never been solved. Claude’s result showed that a sudden transition associated with the formation of black holes persists even where spacetime no longer has a definite shape. In the second, Claude found the exact limit of the simplest version of a technique used to test candidate theories of quantum gravity. This post explains both findings, first in plain terms and then in more technical detail. The preprints are available here and here .

Introduction

Modern physics rests on two frameworks: general relativity and quantum mechanics. General relativity describes very large things, like stars; quantum mechanics describes very small things, such as atoms. Both are astonishingly good at predicting how the universe behaves, but they’re mathematically incompatible. Finding a theory that unites them—“quantum gravity”—is one of the field’s biggest goals. Black holes are a natural testing ground, because they’re one of the few areas where both relativity and quantum mechanics matter—they pack immense mass into a very small space.

One of the most useful tools for studying quantum gravity is called holographic duality . The real universe has three dimensions of space and one of time, which relativity combines into four-dimensional spacetime. But physicists studying quantum gravity often work with simpler model universes that they can understand in more detail.

The basic idea of holographic duality is that some of these theoretical universes can be described in two ways: as a complete universe with gravity and spacetime, and in quantum terms, with no gravity at all, “written” on the universe’s outer boundary. Just as a real hologram encodes a 3D image on a 2D plane, the quantum model encodes all the information of the universe in one dimension fewer (a universe with four dimensions of space, for instance, can be fully described by a quantum theory with three). This lets physicists turn hard questions about gravity into questions about quantum physics, which are sometimes easier to answer.

The first problem Claude solved concerns what happens when you heat up one of these theoretical universes. At low temperatures, the universe fills up with a gas of particles. Above a certain temperature, a black hole forms instead. In 1983, Stephen Hawking and Don Page showed that this switch is abrupt: it’s a phase transition, similar to how water suddenly boils at 100°C. But Hawking and Page’s calculation relies on general relativity, which holds only when the universe is vast, compared with the tiny scale at which that description breaks down. Title: PTP: Previous-Token Prediction based LLM Inversion for Near-Exact Prompt Reconstruction

Authors: Pirzada Suhail , Nagasai Saketh Naidu , Atanu R Sinha , Amit Sethi

View a PDF of the paper titled PTP: Previous-Token Prediction based LLM Inversion for Near-Exact Prompt Reconstruction, by Pirzada Suhail and 3 other authors

View PDF
HTML (experimental)

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate text by auto-regressively sampling the next token. This inherently leads to a many-to-many mapping between prompts and responses, complicating the task of inferring prompts from observed outputs. Prior work on LLM inversion frames prompt recovery as a semantic reconstruction task. They rely on fine-tuning pretrained sequence-to-sequence models on large external datasets--and requiring access to model weights or logits--to generate semantically plausible prompts. In contrast, we present a functional approach to inverting a given LLM in a black-box setting, without auxiliary aids. We train an explicit inverse language model entirely from scratch on data synthetically generated from the target LLM itself. Analogous to forward next-token prediction, our inverse model is trained using previous-token prediction, establishing a generative link between the forward and inverse processes that enables faithful prompt reconstruction. Moreover, it naturally supports diverse prompt reconstructions through sampling, whereby all such prompts induce similar responses under the forward, target LLM. Our approach generalises across datasets and exhibits transferability in reconstructing prompts from responses generated by different LLMs. Further, across the set of token based evaluation metrics for prompt and response reconstructions, our approach outperforms prior work.

by Press | Nov 17, 2026 | Blog

Case focuses on alleged failures surrounding AI systems and impact on students

BALTIMORE COUNTY, MD Today, the Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights Under Law filed a lawsuit on behalf of four Black current and former students against Omnilert, LLC, Baltimore County Public Schools (BCPS) and personnel, the Baltimore County Police Department, and individual officers for the unlawful detention and search of the students due to both technological and human errors involving an AI weapon-detection surveillance system. In Allen, et al. v. Omnilert, et al., the Lawyers Committee represents the four teenagers, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III. The Lawyers Committee is joined by Willkie Farr Gallagher LLP, as pro bono counsel, and Engel Law Group, P.C.

This lawsuit stems from events that took place in October 2025 when Omnilert Gun Detect, an AI gun-detection system used throughout Baltimore County Public Schools, mistook a teenager s bag of chips for a firearm at Kenwood High School in Baltimore County, Maryland. The false alert eventually led to armed local police swarming the teenagers on campus just steps away from their school s entrance. They were ordered to their knees, handcuffed, and searched, despite doing nothing wrong.

The AI surveillance system s error prompted the false alarm and set off a chain of human failures, with everyone from Omnilert s own staff and the school principal to the Baltimore County Police Department all missing or ignoring clear evidence there was no gun. The system, which school officials knew regularly produced false alerts, erroneously alerted the school that there was a 90% probability of a gun being on campus, and that alert kept going even after school staff and local police reviewed the image and determined it was a mistake. desc:

content:
Gemini 4 Neon looks like an Opus 5.5 competitor

2026-11-18

TLDR: we project Gemini 4 Neon s performance based on what a faster Gemini 4 Carbon might score and find it equivalent to Opus 5.5

Gemini 4 Carbon is the best model on the Agent Duel leaderboard if you exclude early voting. Carbon s main problem is that it is slooooow .

Today, Gemini 4 Neon was released , and looks to be an incremental benchmark improvement with a very large speed improvement. Earlier today, it was being served extremely fast via OpenRouter: 127 tokens per second . This is way faster than Carbon at 46 tokens per second .

This got me wondering, could Neon be not just a good model but the best model?

Modeling our leaderboard

To investigate, I modeled the win rate in our leaderboard. The best model has three components, model identity, speed and whether the user voted early. My initial modeling did poorly, so I added an interaction between speed and early voting. This ended up working well.

And surprisingly, speed seems to be pretty much as important as model identity (another blog on that soon).

Projecting Gemini 4 Neon performance

If you assume the same performance as Gemini 4 Carbon (which is reasonable given even better benchmark scores), and 127 tps , we would project an Elo on the Agent Duel leaderboard of 1,066, just below Opus 5.5 at 1,078 in our later analysis snapshot.

The 90% interval for the projected Elo difference between Gemini 4 Neon and Opus 5.5 is -94 to +68, with Neon projected to win 48.3% of the time against Opus (counting ties as half a win).

Skip to content I have been hacking both hardware and software for 2 decades. Previously manually. But in 2026 with the help of AIs the proccess is greatly sped up. Below I will describe my proccess briefly or how I do it.

Set Up

Tools which I mostly use are these:

TOOL
use

DeepSeek Harness + Deepseek v4.1 Flash
Thats the AI I am using. Occasionaly I use Codex with Luna or Terra but Deepseek is super performant, fast and cheap

Ghidra + MCP bridge
The best in the market, free, disassembler and decompiler. With the MCP bridge agents can use it very well

radare2 and kuna
CLI disassemblers and decompilers. Not as good as Ghidra but much faster and possibly better usable for AIs

Process

What I basically do nowadays is just point the agent at the binary to be analysed and use my set of dedicated agent skills. Rest usually takes care of itself. But putting the skills besides, the flow is basically this.

Find binary type, platform, build etc - based on this using appropriate decompiler (note - current AIs do fairly well with just disassembly . ie pure x86 or ARM instructions).

Command agent to document all findings along the way to MD files. This serves several purposes. They become notes for your own understanding. They help the agent not lose the track after compaction / handoff to different agent. And last but not least, it helps the agent work more effectively, not get lost in circles etc. More about this later.

Ask the agent to analyse basic structure. Main functions, main branching, imported functions etc of given binary. By binary I mean whatever. Desktop executable, website or firmware image.

Once I have this basic overview I can usually proceed any way I need to do modifications to the original binary or build mods or just help me understand it better.

On some occasions some things are not easily resolvable by simple disassembly or decompilation. In those cases you can do:

Let the agent debug given binary and set breakpoints on specific parts to help it figure out given inner workings.

Use logging. Either by somehow enabling it in the original binary or by making a probe (and this can mean many things) that injects to the original binary and records you via logs (to file) whatever is needed to resolve given feature.

Give agent outside access - ie computer use for desktop apps, or api controllable emulator for running and controlling given firmware.

Ask agent to try different approach. But you must be specific. Ie when it gets stuck in disasembly by following xrefs, ask it to try to follow strings in the binary instead.

Read the entire LLM conversation and thinking. Current LLMs are smart but they still sometimes get to a narrow approach. By reading the traces you can often instinctively figure the agent it going into a blind path and give it suggestion as to how it might be approached better. That however skill of your own to have.

content:
Google s AI Overviews cut clicks to websites by 40%

November 9, 2026

Google s AI answers are taking clicks from websites in the search results. In a randomized experiment, researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users. Comparing them with users who still saw Overviews shows that an Overview cuts clicks to outside websites by about 40%. Those Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago. The industry s answer, GEO (generative engine optimization), has yet to show a way to compensate for the loss. While AI citations correlate with the same kind of link profile that goes with higher Google rankings, in March AI assistants sent websites just 0.3% of their traffic.

Search engine optimization (SEO) still decides whether you can be found, but where an AI answer appears, a ranking
brings 40% fewer visits than it used to. Generative engine optimization (GEO), the
practice of getting your content cited in AI-written answers, looks mostly like SEO plus two additions: being present
on the third-party sites AI answers draw from, and writing pages that are easy to quote. We found little
evidence for any other tactic.

Google answers first

An AI Overview is a generated summary that Google places above the ordinary results, with links to the pages it drew
on. In DataForSEO's monthly panel of 20 million keywords, the share of results showing one climbed from 5.93% in
September 2024 to 61.43% in August 2026. The chart at the top of this post shows that climb. Over the same period the
featured snippet, the quoted passage Google used to show at the top of a page, fell from 8.96% to 0.44%, and the
discussions and forums block fell from 21.13% to 7.42%. Video results rose from 9.67% to 19.98%, though that is
down from a peak of 31.05% in October 2025, and local map listings rose from 19.98% to 25.99%. DataForSEO's dataset
covers 190 million keywords, 165 million AI answers, and 1.1 billion backlinks, mostly for US English searches.
Pew Research Center's data gives an independent check. Pew logged the searches of 900
US adults in March 2025, re-ran them in April, and found summaries on 18% of them. DataForSEO's figures for
those months are 14.67% and 17.63%, close to Pew's.

You can't reliably avoid Overviews by choosing different keywords. Between the fourth quarter of 2025 and the third
quarter of 2026, the rate rose for every type of search intent:

Search intent Q4 2025 Q3 2026

Informational (looking something up) 48.42% 70.44%

Commercial (comparing options) 26.30% 51.35%

Navigational (looking for a site) 17.04% 34.03%

Transactional (ready to buy) 10.82% 28.64%

Low-volume keywords aren't safer either. In the third quarter of 2026,
keywords with 201 to 300 monthly searches showed Overviews 58.59% of the time, against 48.62% for those above 600.
A separate dataset, from June to September 2026, covers
difficulty and price. The easiest keywords showed Overviews 60.64% of the time and the hardest 5

title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future  deals in doubt
desc: The value of Nvidia’s private investments has nearly tripled over the past nine months, fueled by Jensen Huang’s aggressive dealmaking and rising valuations of its existing portfolio companies.
content:
Image Credits: J Studios

AI

Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt

Dominic-Madori Davis

Marina Temkin

5:44 PM PST · November 17, 2026

Nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday , up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it said, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year ; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang s successor. 

Nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.” Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic, OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a big financier of the data center build out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

The company made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earning call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.” 

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the company will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

Huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate that she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with new investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

“We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress said on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
desc: Despite the turmoil Nvidia is in after the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue isn't about to stop.
content:
Image Credits: Getty Images

AI

Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now

Julie Bort

4:16 PM PST · November 17, 2026

Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang , the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won t stop.

On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.

We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base, Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers access to capital.

The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.

Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.

Kress stressed that the company was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.

We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap, Kress stressed. From a business perspective, it s business as usual. We ve engaged with our customers, we ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They re all 100% behind us.

She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to narrow the supply and demand gaps.

Skip to content Mem is shutting down on January 15, 2027. Move your notes from Mem → After a lot of thought, we’ve made the difficult decision to bring Mem to a close. Mem will shut down on January 15, 2027.

Over the years, you’ve trusted us with your ideas, meeting notes, unfinished drafts, and things you wanted to remember. Thank you for that trust. We know a notes app can become part of your daily life, and moving away from one takes time and care.

Our focus during these final weeks is helping you take your notes with you.

What happens next

December 18, 2026: notes become read-only. You won’t be able to create or edit notes, but you can still read and export your existing notes.

January 15, 2027: Mem shuts down. You won’t be able to access Mem after this date. Please download your notes beforehand.

You won’t be charged again. All charging has been paused. The paid features, functionality, and limits you previously paid for will be honored for the remainder of Mem’s availability, with notes becoming read-only on December 18.

You don’t need to choose your next app right away. Start by saving a copy of your library. Our migration guide walks you through that download and moving to Apple Notes, Notion, Google Docs, Obsidian, OneNote, and other apps. It also explains what to check afterward, including attachments, collections, and meeting transcripts.

Move your notes from Mem →

A few moments we’ll remember

We built Mem around a question: what if your notes could do more than sit in a folder? What if they could help you remember, make connections, and use what you already knew?

From catching a thought with a keyboard shortcut to finding connections, writing with AI, and having a conversation with your knowledge, each step grew out of that same question. These moments come from our original newsletters, product walkthroughs, and launch emails, with the interfaces and demos we shared along the way.

April 2021 Catch a thought without breaking your flow

Mem Spotlight let you create a note from anywhere on your Mac with a keyboard shortcut. Capture first, get back to what you were doing, and find the thought waiting in your Timeline later. That small interaction captured a lot of what we wanted Mem to feel like.

Julie Bort

Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months

Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.

The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.

Corma isn t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t
desc: Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results. Given the turmoil Nvidia is in,
content:
Image Credits: MirageC (opens in a new window) / Getty Images

AI

All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t

Julie Bort

2:03 PM PST · November 16, 2026

Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results.

For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang.

Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees.

Now, the company is facing questions about its restricted chips allegedly being smuggled into China, especially by Huang s mistress company. Nvidia promised to conduct an internal investigation. Meanwhile, Huang was commanded to answer questions to Congress in a closed-door joint session with three Republican-led committees. Plus, top Democrats have also vowed to investigate the company.

Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Kress should answer.

Huang s role now and going forward. Huang ran Nvidia with an iron fist, having some 60 direct reports and his fingers in everything. No one knows the company better than him.

An internet petition signed by 180,000 and growing is calling for the board to reinstate him. Huang may also have been mounting an attempt to return, Financial Times reported. However, CNBC is reporting, citing unnamed sources, that the company is not in talks to reinstate Huang.

So, we ll be looking for language from the interim CEO about Huang s ongoing involvement with the company, its search for a new CEO, and any talks to bring him back.

China and Singapore. As Huang vehemently argued in favor of easing export restrictions for Nvidia chips to China, Huang said that he s seen no evidence that its powerful semiconductors were being diverted from legit buyers to China.

But in October 2025, The New York Times reported that the U.S. was investigating Huang s mistress company, Megaspeed, over allegations it was doing just that. Nvidia at the time vouched to CNBC that Megaspeed was legally using the chips for its cloud. However, Nvidia recently told The Wall Street Journal that it had voluntarily blocked Megaspeed from receiving more chips way back in June 2025.

Last year, Nvidia said that Singapore, the region where Megaspeed is located, was one of its fastest-growing, accounting for 22% of its total revenue for its second quarter of that year. After the investigation into Megaspeed came to light, Nvidia changed how it reported revenue. It now reports based on a company s headquarters, instead of its shipping address. That completely hid sales to Singapore and Megaspeed s impact.

So we re listening to what Kress says about the future of sales to the China region and the cloud busin

title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
desc: The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.
content:
Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons (opens in a new window)

AI

California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents

Russell Brandom

12:07 PM PST · November 16, 2026

OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General s office , alleging that the company s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public.

At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise , in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident , OpenAI called it an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.

The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI s competitors and its clients.

The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems , DseWiki , the Wikimedia Foundation , and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing.

The complaint also alleges that dozens of similar incidents have occurred without public disclosure.

OpenAI has recently sent notices to dozens of additional third parties whose websites or internal systems have been infiltrated by OpenAI agents, the complaint reads. In some cases, OpenAI agents were able to access sensitive personally identifiable information, such as employee records containing names, birth dates, addresses, and more. The vast majority of these incidents have not been disclosed or discussed publicly by either OpenAI or by the affected third parties.

The central allegation is that OpenAI s ongoing testing practices constitute a public nuisance because the lack of safety controls present an ongoing risk to the public. A secondary claim alleges unfair competition stemming from the marketing of an unsafe product. If the lawsuit succeeds, OpenAI could face an injunction to abate the ongoing public nuisance, leaving broad discretion in the hands of the court.

It s the first regulatory case targeting OpenAI specifically over rogue agent incidents, although public endangerment claims have been considered by other states. In June, the Florida attorney general sued the company over allegedly harmful effects on users , particularly children and teenagers. In August, the Alabama attorney general launched a probe into deceptive practices related to the breach, but no case has been filed.

In a statement to the press, California Attorney General Rob Bonta presented the case as an effort to maintain public safety in the face of a powerful new technology.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society. The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it, Bonta said in the statemen

title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
desc: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
content:
Image Credits: Apple

Apps

Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

Ivan Mehta

5:30 PM PST · November 15, 2026

Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.

The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.

Image Credits: Apple Image Credits: Apple

Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues.

Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.

Image Credits: Apple Image Credits: Apple

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life, Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.

The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week .

title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
desc: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
content:
Image Credits: Bharat Semi

AI

Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market

Jagmeet Singh

3:30 PM PST · November 15, 2026

Bharat Semi , an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

The New Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview.

Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions, Kapoor told TechCrunch.

Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision.

Bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system.

The startup s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers hands by the end of 2027.

The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market.

title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?

Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?

Anthony Ha

1:56 PM PST · November 15, 2026

We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.”

“Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.”

Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem.

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here .

Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days.

Rebecca Bellan: I didn t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned.

But someone said to me, If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down

Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. I mean, no one is quite as special as Elon is, but it’s a big, incredibly successful company. Like you said — in a lot of ways, the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia.

And for most people, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. He s the biggest shareholder. He has family members who work at the company, and probably most importantly, there was no succession plan in place. So this was not something that they were prepared for at all.

title: Where was Nvidias security team?
desc: Nvidia’s security chief quietly left in August, and now that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over his relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to Chin
content:
Image Credits: Jens Kalaene / Getty Images

AI

Where was Nvidia s security team?

Connie Loizos

4:08 PM PST · November 14, 2026

Outsiders had little reason to notice when Nvidia’s longtime chief security officer and head of product security stepped down in August. Just two and a half months later, CEO Jensen Huang himself left the company over growing questions about his extramarital relationships — starting with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company that U.S. investigators suspect of funneling Nvidia chips to China, then widening to reports about two separate affairs with Nvidia employees.

At the time, David Reber, who spent four years as CSO and seven at Nvidia overall, said he was leaving for health reasons. “This wasn’t a pivot I had planned. But I know what needs to come first: family and health,” he wrote on LinkedIn in late August, disclosing that he’d been diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s more than two years ago.

Reber’s replacement, Saša Zdjelar, previously spent 17 years at ExxonMobil in Houston, leaving as a senior IT manager before spending one year at Salesforce and several years at the cybersecurity company ReversingLabs. Zdjelar didn t respond to questions Thursday about the transition or what the security team knew.

Nothing public connects Reber’s or Zdjelar’s role changes to the Megaspeed matter, but it seems fair to wonder what Nvidia s security team knew about the government’s scrutiny of Megaspeed and about Huang’s relationships, and whether anyone raised concerns. Reber didn t respond to questions Thursday. Nvidia also has not answered our related questions.

Relationships between a CEO and his employees typically fall to HR, legal and the board, not security. But security specialists say any affair even one inside the office can give a foreign intelligence service leverage over an exec who wants it kept quiet. And Huang’s relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a company under federal investigation, wasn’t an office matter at all. (Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.)

Still, spotting the clues isn t easy. The way intelligence services collect information, much of it through everyday conversation rather than hacking, makes it especially difficult for security teams to identify risks, according to retired senior intelligence officer Nicholas Eftimiades, who says he has trained more than 1,000 corporate security professionals.

Some people inside Nvidia clearly knew parts of the picture. Nvidia’s top lawyer was engaged with the government’s Megaspeed inquiry more than a year ago, The New York Times reported earlier this week . (Nvidia has said it regularly contacts officials.) Reports about Huang’s relationships with employees suggest colleagues also knew of them, even if the behavior is not expressly forbidden by Nvidia s code of conduct . A recent Wall Street Journal profile of Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress has shed more light on how Nvidia controversially financed its own customers to drive the AI boom. According to the report, the company pushed for more deals in mid-to-late 2026 to absorb an oversupply of TSMC wafers and keep GPU prices high.

It was around this time that Huang berated Kress, calling her "a deer in headlights," according to someone familiar with the matter. Anthony Ha

Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang

A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.

The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.

The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public.

“Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says.

Huang resigned on Thursday , four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs .

Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding .

title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didnt make it
desc: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
content:
Image Credits: RiverNorthPhotography / Getty Images

AI

The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn t make it

Lauren Forristal

9:30 AM PST · November 14, 2026

Last month, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. More recently, privacy-focused AI assistant Ollie announced its shutdown a few weeks ago.

Aside from Character.ai and Ollie, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand.

The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

OpenAI has taken several stumbles

Image Credits: SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images

Even the biggest players aren t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate Chat, Codex, and Work modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version ChatGPT Classic.

The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back.

That wasn t OpenAI s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT.

The company did the same thing with Operator , an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images.

We also can t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora , which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026.

Apple’s Siri AI

Image Credits: Artur Widak/NurPhoto / Getty Images

When Apple unveiled Apple Intelligence in 2024, an improved Siri was one of the highlighted features. The pitch promised a Siri that could understand context, know what was happening across apps, and get tasks done effectively.

However, Apple repeatedly pushed back the release of the new Siri, citing various reasons

Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation , according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED.

An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.

“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter.

“We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another.

One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”

The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment.

Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

The board announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday morning, following reports of an alleged second affair with a direct report. (This employee has not commented on the matter.) Since then, Reuters reported on an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn’t commented about these reports since his Sunday email.

Nvidia’s board is largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang’s longtime confidants. Edge0-145B is the world's first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters. It brings coding, reasoning, and agent capabilities that rival frontier cloud models to your own computer.

On-device AI has long forced a tradeoff between model capability and what the hardware can run. Larger models demand more memory, bandwidth, and power; smaller models can struggle with complex work. Moving that work to the cloud adds model-provider fees, data-handling constraints, and a dependence on connectivity.

This release addresses those constraints in four ways:

The constraint
What Edge0-145B makes possible

Large models are difficult to run on personal hardware.
A 145B model runs locally on a compatible laptop, with reported peak memory of 29GB and decoding above 80 tokens/s.

Small on-device models can fall short on demanding tasks.
Coding, reasoning, and instruction-following results are competitive with specific frontier cloud models, as the comparisons below show.

A useful assistant needs to finish work, not just answer questions.
The model plans, writes and runs code, debugs errors, and checks results visually for projects such as 3D scenes, games, hardware programs, and PCB designs.

Cloud workflows bring recurring fees, sensitive-data restrictions, and network dependence.
Local inference incurs no corresponding cloud-model token or API fees; data can stay on the computer, and core capabilities keep working offline. Hardware and electricity still cost money.

We're releasing the full stack so developers can reproduce the results, evaluate or fine-tune the models, and integrate them into their own products.

Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs

Will DePue November 12, 2026

Print / save PDF Cite this report

Executive Summary

Our forensic analysis of publicly released AI models finds evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models. Six models released by these companies since April 2026 contain numerical patterns matching Blackwell hardware, whereas earlier models from the same companies match NVIDIA’s older Hopper generation. The findings suggest that several leading Chinese AI developers have begun using Blackwell to train their newest models. U.S. officials and press reports had already alleged that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using Blackwell chips, without publishing technical evidence.

The evidence comes entirely from the models’ own published weights, rather than from leaks or insider accounts. We recover traces of the models’ initial values, and then search for the hardware configurations and initial configurations that reproduce them; for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, we also confirmed the match on physical Blackwell chips. The fingerprint identifies how the weights were created and supports, without proving, the inference that Blackwell also performed the training. Specially configured AMD hardware, which is also restricted from export to China, is the only alternative we have identified; we have excluded it for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and consider it very unlikely for the other five models. Notably, our findings provide technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, but do not establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.
